reviewer_note: Loom is not applicable: IPC server uses sequential I/O, not concurrent memory ordering. No lock-free structures, no atomic operations, no channel interleavings.
Miri is not applicable: vb_ipc crate uses #![forbid(unsafe_code)]. All byte reads go through safe std::io::Read and byteorder traits. No raw pointers, no MaybeUninit, no aliasing, no UB.
Flux RS refinement types not yet in project scope. Decode order theorem proven adequately via Kani (exhaustive) + Verus (refinement proof).

Cargo-fuzz would fuzz byte-level input at the frame boundary. However, Kani already exhausts all 2^192 possible 24-byte header combinations. Byte-level fuzz would not add coverage beyond Kani exhaustive check. Cargo-fuzz is not a substitute for exhaustive model checking on this input domain.
